analysis.title: AI: The next squeeze or the next regime shift?
key_insights: Goldman prime brokerage data shows US technology long/short positioning at its lowest level since records began in 2016. The selling has shifted from long liquidation and de-grossing to outright short building.
CTAs have aggressively sold technology, with Nasdaq positioning back near maximum short levels. This leaves room for a sharp short squeeze.
The note separates a positioning-driven rebound, which needs only better sentiment, from a genuine return of AI leadership, which needs renewed confidence in earnings and financing.
Semiconductors have underperformed the S&P 500 by more than 30 percentage points since June, the sharpest relative drawdown since 2002.

Goldman's AI semiconductor basket trades at 11x 2028 earnings versus nearly 16x for the S&P 500, while consensus forecasts 31% earnings growth in 2028. At the S&P multiple, the price implies roughly a 6% earnings decline.

Goldman argues parts of the AI complex price in excessive downward revisions to 2027 earnings. Korean memory stocks are priced near the bearish end of the earnings scenario range, and some memory names could potentially double if confidence returns.

The correlation between three-month and twelve-month momentum has turned negative. AI names have moved into the short legs of shorter-term momentum strategies. Tech is sold by 3- and 6-month momentum but remains a modest buy in 12-month momentum.
Momentum volatility is running at 3.5 times that of the S&P 500, so sharp rotations and reversals could persist.

Goldman estimates that even in a bearish scenario, new data center capacity coming online in 2028 stays roughly in line with 2027, with potential upside of more than 50% if more projects proceed. The constraint is financing, as AI companies want to spend more than their cash generation while borrowing costs rise.

Goldman's 2027 outlook has AI spending continuing to grow but its growth rate possibly peaking early next year. AI has contributed more to corporate earnings and equity performance than to GDP, so slower spending growth could hurt stocks more than the economy.

The largest index weights increasingly lack free cash flow, and non-cash earnings are a growing share of earnings growth. Goldman's US High versus Low Free Cash Flow basket has been outperforming, with gains driven equally by the long and short legs.
The S&P 500 excluding AI has outperformed the broader index over the past year and held up better in last week's sell-off.

The STOXX Europe 600 has a two-year daily beta of less than 0.05 to Goldman's US AI basket. European companies with high and stable margins are starting to break out, and the note frames this as a possible diversification flow into Europe.

tension_points.bull_case: Record bearish tech positioning, short building, and semis priced for an earnings decline (11x 2028 earnings vs nearly 16x for the S&P) leave room for a violent squeeze, with Korean memory names potentially doubling.
tension_points.bear_case: A rebound may be positioning-driven only. Financing constraints, a possible early-2027 peak in AI spending growth, and negative momentum signals could mean AI's leadership regime has changed.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Renewed confidence in earnings and financing would validate a lasting return of AI leadership. Without it, a rebound is only a positioning squeeze.
